title.narrative: OECD: Just transition in the Western Balkans
OECD: Rättvis energiomställning på västra Balkan

description.narrative:
Deliverable project objectives
The project aims to assist the Western Balkans in creating conditions for low-carbon and socially inclusive development by:
- Generating concrete policy options for coordinated energy sector, social protection and fiscal reforms to reduce the environmental impact of development in the Western Balkans while fostering more inclusive growth.
- Generating estimates of the potential for green job creation and recommendations for creating a supportive environment for the creation of green jobs.
- Creating a push for implementation through peer-learning exchange that brings together key policy makers and experts from the region and beyond, relevant to coordinated energy sector, social protection and fiscal reforms.
The project will combine country-based analysis with regional analysis and peer-learning activities. It will cover Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia, and Serbia.
Intermediate project goals
The above is supported by the following intermediate goals:
1. Establish the evidence base on energy subsidies in the region through:
- A systematic overview of energy subsidies and estimates of their economic and distributional impact.
- Estimates of the incidence of various combinations of energy subsidy/price reform, with indications of winners and losers across multiple dimensions (income level, geographical location, household composition).
2. Build key tools for policy analysis and design of energy subsidy reform and green job policies, including:
- Micro-simulation models to generate distributional estimates of impact.
- Macro models to assess the impact of energy reforms on the labour market by simulating reform scenarios (including new investment into renewable energy), to identify which sectors and workers are most affected.
3. Generate policy recommendations in consultation with the economies of the region for a coordinated energy, social protection and fiscal reform based on the OECD analysis, as well as national and regional peer-learning outcomes.

Insatsen "Just transition in the Western Balkans: Supporting coordinated energy sector, social protection and fiscal reform" genomfört av Organisationen för ekonomiskt samarbete och utveckling (OECD) Development Centre bygger på The Multi-dimensional Review of the Western Balkan (2021, 2022) och syftar till att stödja västra Balkan (Albanien, Bosnien och Hercegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, Nordmakedonien och Serbien) att skapa förutsättningar för en koldioxidsnål och socialt inkluderande utveckling. Insatsen vill generera konkreta politiska alternativ och en push för deras genomförande genom regionalt utbyte och lärande.

The project “Just transition in the Western Balkans through coordinated energy sector, social protection and fiscal reform” implemented by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) Development Centre builds on The Multi-dimensional Review of the Western Balkans (2021, 2022) and aims to support the Western Balkans (Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia and Serbia) create conditions for a low-carbon and socially inclusive development. The contribution aims to generate concrete policy options and a push for their implementation through regional peer-learning and exchange.

sector.narrative: Energy sector policy, planning and administration

description.narrative:
From 1 December 2022 to 14 June 2024, the OECD reported achieving the following two outcomes:
1. Creating a knowledge base and analytical tools as basis for reforms for achieving a just green transition: With the completion of full inventory of energy subsidies and support measures, the project has made a significant contribution to the evidence base in the region on the full costs of current energy sector and the implications for each country's public finances. With different economic models the project has created important tools that will support the following peer learning phase and can continue to serve energy policy makers in the region.
2. Securing buy-in from a large network of stakeholders across the region: Through multiple visits to the project countries and consultation meetings, as well as the meeting of the Mutual Learning Group in Paris, the project has been able to generate support from counterparts in all governments, as well as a network of relevant stakeholders across Western Balkans that will participate in the peer learning phase. This is an important prerequisite for a successful peer learning phase that has the objective to generate evidence based action.
The risk related to lack of (or insufficient quality of) necessary data obtained from countries did materialize during the analytical phase, causing several delays for data processing and analysis, and subsequently for the start of the peer learning phase.
The interim regional report was presented and discussed at the informal meeting of the OECD Mutual Learning Group on 14 June 2024. The meeting brought together ambassadors, experts and policy makers from the Western Balkans and OECD Development Centres member countries. It featured a presentation of the analytical findings of the project, which was positively received by all stakeholders. Sida participated also in the meeting..
